**Name:** _________________________________________   

## Goal

Test whether a **per-person limit** improves sustainability, fairness, and compliance.

## Materials (Instructor provides)

- Reset lake to **30 fish**.
- Same 8 boats (cups).

> **Biological Rule**  
> After harvest, fish remaining in the lake **double** (up to **30**).

## Communication Rules (Read aloud & follow exactly)

- **Discussion Allowed (2 minutes)** to agree on **one per-person limit** (e.g., “2 fish per fisher”).
- After the 2-minute discussion ends, **no further discussion** or signaling. Everyone must follow the same per-person limit exactly.

::: callout-note

### You may communicate (for 2 minutes max):

- Propose and agree on a **per-person limit**.

### You must NOT:

- Exceed the agreed per-person limit.
- Signal or negotiate during harvesting.

:::

## Procedure

1. **Set the Per-Person Limit (group, 2 minutes):**  
   **Per-person limit =** _________ fish
2. **Harvest Exactly the Limit:** When the instructor says “**Fish!**” each fisher takes exactly the agreed limit.
3. **Reproduction:** Instructor counts remaining fish and **doubles** them (up to 30).
4. **Record** your results.

### Data Table (Round 3)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Agreed per-person limit |  |
| Total class catch (limit × 8) |  |
| Fish remaining after harvest |  |
| Fish after reproduction (doubled, max 30) |  |

## Individual Reflection (submit with this handout)

1. Was cooperation easier with a per-person rule? Why or why not?\bigskip\bigskip\bigskip
2. Did this round appear more sustainable than Round 1 and/or Round 2? Briefly explain.\bigskip\bigskip\bigskip
3. Which system felt **most fair** to you: Open Access, Fixed Quota, or Fixed Effort? Why?\bigskip\bigskip\bigskip
4. Name **one** real-world example where a per-person (effort) limit is used.\bigskip\bigskip\bigskip
